comment_boxes.NodeComment: Forces Refresh when base terrain changes
Filter for Elements that dont follow the terrain slope

graph_props.Description: This PCG will spawn the ground assets, Including Sidewalk and ground tiles.

nodes.comment: slight expansion to ensure good coverage under the sidewalk
nodes.name: Subgraph_10
nodes.title: Expanded unbuildable footprints

nodes.comment:
Extracts straight edge segments from lot boundary polygons (angle threshold 20°).
These segments are the input splines for the sidewalk grammar assignment.
nodes.name: Subgraph_8
nodes.title: Extract Lot Edge Segments (Sidewalk)

nodes.comment:
First of a 7-way sequential random cull chain. Each stage culls a fraction
of the remaining points so that every tile variant receives an equal 1/7 share:
  Stage 1: 1/7  (ratio=0.1429)
  Stage 2: 1/6 of remainder = 1/7  (ratio=0.1667)
  Stage 3: 1/5 of remainder = 1/7  (ratio=0.2000)
  Stage 4: 1/4 of remainder = 1/7  (ratio=0.2500)
  Stage 5: 1/3 of remainder = 1/7  (ratio=0.3333)
  Stage 6: 1/2 of remainder = 1/7  (ratio=0.5000 — implicit, remainder split)
  Stage 7: all remaining points
Each Selected output feeds one Spawn node (A–G).
nodes.name: FC_RandomChoice_1
nodes.title: Random Choice 1/7

nodes.comment:
Lifts tile placement points 15 units above the nominal ground plane
so the subsequent terrain projector can snap them cleanly to the surface
without z-fighting or missed hits from below.
nodes.name: Subgraph_33
nodes.title: Lift Ground Tile Points +15 (Pre-Projection)

nodes.comment:
Extracts the ArteryWidth attribute value from the road polygon data
and promotes it to element domain so it can be used as a scalar
input to the city shape expansion node.
nodes.name: ExtractAttribute_1
nodes.title: Extract ArteryWidth From Road Polygon

nodes.comment:
Halves the artery road width to get the sidewalk expansion distance.
The city shape is expanded by this amount so the sidewalk outer edge
aligns with the road centreline offset.
nodes.name: AttributeMathsOp_1
nodes.title: ArteryWidth / 2 (Sidewalk Expansion Amount)

nodes.comment:
Expands the city shape polygon outward by half the artery road width.
This defines the outer extent of the sidewalk placement zone,
matching the road edge so sidewalks align with road geometry.
nodes.name: Subgraph_23
nodes.title: Expand City Shape By Half Artery Width (Sidewalk Zone)

nodes.comment:
Assigns SGD_Sidewalk_Corners grammar to contracted lot boundary segments.
spawnAssets=false — spawning happens in Spawn Corner Assets after projection.
Heavy because corner detection runs on every lot boundary in the city.
nodes.name: Subgraph_26
nodes.title: Assign Corners

nodes.comment:
Removes undividable district areas and the landmark small park spline
from the lot polygons, leaving only the tile-able ground footprint.
nodes.name: Subgraph_7
nodes.title: Exclude Undividable Districts And Landmark Park

nodes.comment:
Produces the polygon area where lots border undividable districts.
This boundary is where the railing/fence grammar will be placed
to define the edge between buildable and non-buildable zones.
nodes.name: Subgraph_14
nodes.title: Intersect Lots With Undividable Districts (Railing Zone)

nodes.comment:
Assigns inline grammar [[C,P]10,empty]* to the railing boundary segments.
Alternates railing sections (C=SM_Railing_A, P=SM_Fence_Post_A01) in groups
of 10, separated by empty gaps of 250 units for visual variation.
nodes.name: Subgraph_20
nodes.title: Assign Railing And Fence Grammar

nodes.comment:
Removes the landmark footprint from the railing boundary area.
The landmark has its own boundary treatment — railing should not
be placed where the landmark polygon overlaps the district edge.
nodes.name: Subgraph_29
nodes.title: Exclude Landmark From Railing Boundary

nodes.comment:
Assigns SGD_Sidewalk_A grammar to lot edge and landmark edge segments.
spawnAssets=false — actual asset spawning happens in Spawn Sidewalk Assets
after terrain projection. Heavy because it processes all lot edges city-wide.
nodes.name: Subgraph_31
nodes.title: Assign Sidewalks

nodes.comment:
Start of the street prop yaw-correction chain.
The sidewalk grammar spawns street props (lamp posts, hydrants, meters, mailboxes)
via spline placement, which can introduce unwanted Roll and Pitch tilt.
This chain: (1) casts the Asset soft path to a string for substring filtering,
(2) identifies each prop type by asset name, (3) zeroes Roll then Pitch,
(4) re-spawns so props stand perfectly upright regardless of terrain slope.
nodes.name: AttributeCast_0
nodes.title: Cast Asset to String

nodes.comment: Yaw-only: SM_StreetLamp_A_Pole_Large
nodes.name: FilterDataByAttribute_0
nodes.title: Filter: Lamp Post

nodes.comment: Yaw-only: uh4ocfafa_LOD0 (Fire_Hydrant_02)
nodes.name: FilterDataByAttribute_1
nodes.title: Filter: Fire Hydrant

nodes.comment: Yaw-only: ujpkaadfa_LOD0 (Parking_Meter_00)
nodes.name: FilterDataByAttribute_2
nodes.title: Filter: Parking Meter

nodes.comment: Yaw-only: uhcjaisfa_LOD0 (Mailbox_00)
nodes.name: FilterDataByAttribute_3
nodes.title: Filter: Mailbox

nodes.comment:
Sets $Rotation.Roll to 0 on all matched street prop points.
Corrects the roll component introduced by spline-tangent alignment.
nodes.name: AttributeMathsOp_0
nodes.title: Zero Roll On Street Props

nodes.comment:
Sets $Rotation.Pitch to 0 on the roll-corrected street prop points.
After zeroing both Roll and Pitch, props have only a Yaw rotation
so they stand upright while still facing the correct direction.
nodes.name: AttributeMathsOp_3
nodes.title: Zero Pitch On Street Props

nodes.comment:
Filters the Roads PCG output to polygon data only.
The ArteryWidth attribute used for sidewalk zone expansion lives on
the road polygon, not on point or spline data.
nodes.name: FilterDataByTag_4
nodes.title: Filter Road Polygons (Has ArteryWidth Attr)

nodes.comment:
Reverses the city shape boundary spline direction to clockwise.
The sidewalk grammar expects an inward-facing normal, which requires
the boundary to run in the opposite direction to the city shape polygon.
nodes.name: Subgraph_3
nodes.title: Reverse City Boundary Spline

nodes.comment:
Reserved lots are set aside for plazas and must not receive ground tiles.
Excluding them here ensures only buildable, unreserved lots are tiled.
nodes.name: Subgraph_22
nodes.title: Exclude Reserved Lots From Ground Area

nodes.comment:
Extracts edge segments from the contracted landmark boundary (angle threshold 5°).
Tighter threshold than lots because the landmark edge is smoother and needs
finer segment resolution for the sidewalk grammar.
nodes.name: Subgraph_4
nodes.title: Extract Landmark Edge Segments (Sidewalk)

nodes.comment:
Contracts the landmark footprint inward by 300 units to set the sidewalk
edge back from the landmark boundary, preventing sidewalk tiles from
overlapping the landmark polygon.
nodes.name: Subgraph_46
nodes.title: Contract Landmark Boundary (Sidewalk Setback 300)

nodes.comment:
Cuts the reversed city boundary spline at the expanded central park boundary.
This removes the section of boundary that runs through the park,
leaving only the portions where sidewalks should be placed.
nodes.name: Subgraph_49
nodes.title: Cut City Boundary Spline At Central Park

nodes.comment: Expands the central park footprint by 1900 units to create a buffer zone equivalent of the local road width
nodes.name: Subgraph_52
nodes.title: Expand Central Park (Spline Cut Buffer)

nodes.comment: only vehicles
nodes.name: FilterDataByAttribute_4
nodes.title: Filter: vehicles

nodes.comment:
Debug path only — fed by Branch_2 Output B when the debug parameter is enabled.
Assigns SM_Plaza_Square_A across all ground points rather than the randomised split.
nodes.name: AssignGroundTiles_A
nodes.title: Assign Ground Tiles A (Debug)
